subject: Fwd: Inflight exception in SDK + missing telemetry for adaptive-batch path
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finlytics.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching

Hi Maya,

Quick note from our SREs: over the past 48 hours we've seen ~20 errors per hour coming from calls that use the Redwood SDK with prefetch=enabled and adaptive_batching=aggressive. The error is logged as an "inflight exception" at the SDK layer and the call just fails (no token stream). The weird part: your hosted metrics don't show any corresponding kernel failures — there's a gap in telemetry for these requests.

We've attached a debug log and a minimal repro (Node) that triggers 2-3 failures in a short run. Can someone on engineering look? This started after we flipped to the new adaptive-batching policy you recommended last week.

Impact: product demo next Tue; if this persists we need a rollback plan.

Thanks,
Liam
SRE, FinLytics

Attachments: debug-log-2026-10-08.txt, min-repro.zip

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: liam@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-10-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching

Forwarding Liam's message — this came in during onboarding with FinLytics (DL-4821). High priority: they see failures only when prefetch + aggressive adaptive batching are enabled. They also report missing kernel-level telemetry for the failing requests (hosted metrics show a telemetry gap).

Ask: can platform/runtime and SDK teams review the attached logs and the repro and confirm whether this is a runtime fallback, an SDK race condition, or an instrumentation gap? If we need a config-level stopgap (disable prefetch or lower adaptive thresholds), let's propose it.

Next steps I want in 24 hours: 1) quick hypothesis and 2) a short mitigation we can push to the tenant (config toggle) before the demo.

-Maya
Enterprise SE | Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-08T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching

Thanks for the forward. I pulled the attached debug-log and the min-repro — good repro, thanks. Initial observations: the SDK logs an "inflight exception" right after prefetch completes and we attempt to flush the batched request. There are two likely buckets: 1) a race between KV cache refill and batch dispatch (we've seen subtle NPEs there), or 2) an outbound socket reset that the runtime isn't surfacing into our telemetry.

What I need from platform/runtime to prioritize:
- kernel/device-level logs (GPU/driver errors) for the same timestamps (2026-10-07 23:50 -> 2026-10-08 01:00 UTC)
- the request IDs (we can correlate if runtime has them) 

Mitigation we can do quickly on tenant config: set prefetch=disabled for their tenant OR set adaptive_batching.mode=conservative. Both are reversible and safe. Will prepare a short rollback doc.

Dev
Senior SWE, SDK

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-09T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching

Thanks — I pulled runtime traces for the tenant window and correlated with our ingress. Notes:
- There are a handful of requests where the runtime shows "conn-reset" at the transport layer immediately after the prefetch completion. Those same requests do not show kernel OOMs or CUDA errors.
- Telemetry gap appears when requests are handled by the new pooling path (v2-serving-pool) — we forgot to wire request-level IDs into the async dispatch callback for that codepath, so some failures are never propagated to the metric collector. In short: this is an instrumentation gap on v2-serving-pool (INF-9342).

Actionable items:
- Hotfix A: patch v2-serving-pool to always attach request_id before async dispatch (small change). We'll test and can canary to a subset of tenants within 24-36 hours.
- Mitigation B (immediate): disable prefetch for FinLytics tenant (safe) and set adaptive_batching.mode=conservative. This avoids the v2-serving-pool path for problematic requests.
- Long-term: add unit/integration tests that assert request_id propagation for pooled async paths.

I've opened JIRA INF-9342 and attached the traces. Will post the canary plan after Dev confirms SDK-side changes are unnecessary.

Marissa
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-09T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching

Agree with Marissa's diagnosis — it's an instrumentation propagation hole. Quick notes from field:
- We've seen the same symptom on two other customers after they enabled aggressive batching + prefetch. In both cases the visible SDK error is "inflight exception" but runtime shows a transport reset without kernel failures.
- Customer-facing ask: clear explanation + mitigation and a short ETA for the hotfix canary. They need to decide about the demo rollback.

Proposal:
1) Immediate tenant config: Maya, can you confirm if we should toggle prefetch off for FinLytics?
2) Marissa: please ping when INF-9342 has a build. Dev/SDK team: if SDK needs a guard (noop on certain callbacks) let's discuss small release.

Rishi
Staff SE, Field

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: liam@finlytics.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent 'inflight exception' when using SDK prefetch + adaptive batching — MAP and next steps

Hi Liam — thanks again for the repro and patience. Quick update and mutual action plan: 

What we found: Marissa identified an instrumentation gap in the v2-serving-pool that can drop request IDs on async dispatch; when that coincides with aggressive adaptive batching + prefetch the SDK surfaces an "inflight exception" while the runtime shows a transport reset. No kernel-level OOMs detected.

Short-term mitigation (we can apply now):
- We will disable prefetch for your tenant and set adaptive_batching.mode=conservative. This should eliminate the v2-serving-pool codepath that drops request IDs.
- ETA for config change: 1 hour. We'll monitor live traffic for 4 hours and report back.

Medium-term (canary/hotfix):
- Platform will ship INF-9342 hotfix that ensures request_id propagation on v2-serving-pool. Marissa estimates a canary in 24-36 hours, full rollout in ~72 hours pending safety checks.

Owner matrix:
- Apply tenant config toggle: Maya (SE) + Platform ops (Marissa) — target: 2026-10-11T17:00:00-07:00
- Hotfix build and canary: Marissa + runtime team — start: 2026-10-12
- SDK guard review (if needed): Dev Patel — to confirm if any SDK-side defensive logging is required by 2026-10-12T18:00:00-07:00

Ask for you: confirm you want us to proceed with the immediate tenant toggle (reply YES to proceed) or if you'd prefer to rollback adaptive-batching on your side.

We'll follow up once the toggle is applied and again after the canary.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise SE | Redwood Inference
